mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months in at least two out of three such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) in at least three out of five instances following a confirmed GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that elevates wage pressures, prompting the Fed to raise rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) during periods when UNRATE > 4% for two consecutive months in at least three out of five such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE indicates a broad-based employment expansion without wage inflation, which supports corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: expansionary labor market without wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) in at least three out of five instances following the described PAYEMS/UNRATE co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production and reduced corporate earnings capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) in at least three out of five episodes following four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in HOUST above its 52-week moving average for six consecutive months signals robust housing demand, which correlates with consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 52-week MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) in at least four out of six instances following six consecutive months of HOUST above its 52-week MA.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 3% for three consecutive months signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate earnings power and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: simultaneous monetary tightening and inflation acceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 mean excess return) in at least three out of five episodes following the described FEDFUNDS/CPIAUCSL co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in RSAFS above 5% signals robust retail sales momentum, which correlates with stronger consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 mean excess return) in at least six out of ten instances when RSAFS YoY growth exceeds 5%.
